All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed by locals and food‑bloggers alike. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1111 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)

Website: [thethaikitchen.com](https://www.thethaikitchen.com) | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants share the same address (1120 W 18th St) because they are part of the same Thai‑food complex in the West Loop. They each have their own branding and slightly different menus, but they all offer vegetarian options and can accommodate special requests (e.g., no fish sauce, no egg, tofu instead of meat). ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai Food 1. **Ask for “no fish sauce”** – Fish sauce is a staple in Thai cooking, but many restaurants will happily omit it for vegetarian diners. 2. **Request “no egg”** – Some dishes (like Pad Thai or Fried Rice) traditionally contain egg; ask for a “no egg” version. 3. **Choose tofu or tempeh** – These are common protein substitutes in vegetarian Thai dishes. 4. **Vegetable‑heavy curries** – Green, red, or Massaman curries can be made vegetarian with tofu and plenty of veggies. 5. **Spring rolls & salads** – Fresh spring rolls (no shrimp) and papaya salad (no fish sauce) are naturally vegetarian. If you’d like a more specific recommendation (e.g., a place with a dedicated vegetarian menu, or a spot that’s especially popular among vegans), let me know and I can narrow it down further!
